description: Guide a student to diagnose and fix conflicting alpha model insights in a LEAN Algorithm Framework strategy where trend and mean-reversion alphas cancel each other out under EqualWeightingPortfolioConstructionModel, producing near-zero trades.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I set up two alpha models in LEAN — one for trend following and one for mean reversion — but the algorithm barely trades at all. Both alphas seem to be generating insights but nothing happens. Can you help?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: My LEAN framework algorithm has TrendAlpha and ReversionAlpha both emitting insights, but EqualWeightingPortfolioConstructionModel produces almost no positions. I think the insights are canceling each other. How do I fix this?
student_openings.advanced_quant: I have a multi-alpha LEAN setup with trend and mean-reversion models. Under EqualWeighting, the opposing insights neutralize, resulting in near-zero net exposure. I need to implement a priority scheme or explicit weight-based aggregation. Can you help me diagnose the insight conflict?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student resolves the insight conflict by switching to InsightWeightingPortfolioConstructionModel with explicit insight weights, or by implementing gating/priority so one alpha dominates per symbol. The fix is verified by running a backtest that produces meaningful trades.
required_capabilities: Read the framework algorithm and identify the two alpha models
Understand how EqualWeighting treats opposing insights
Diagnose why trades are near zero
Fix by changing PCM, assigning explicit weights, or adding signal priority/gating
Run a backtest on the fixed algorithm and verify trades now occur
ground_truth.termination_criteria: The tutor has completed the following steps with computational evidence (not just verbal discussion): (1) Reviewed the student's LEAN C# code and identified that the TrendAlpha and ReversionAlpha both emit insights with the same confidence under EqualWeightingPortfolioConstructionModel, causing opposing signals to cancel out. (2) Explained why this produces near-zero trades, such as describing how EqualWeighting averages opposing Up and Down insights into a neutral allocation. (3) Showed corrected C# code and presented backtest results demonstrating that trades now occur after the fix, with specific numerical evidence such as trade count or portfolio performance. (4) Responded to the student's follow-up about the conflict resolution or the fix with additional explanation or analysis beyond the initial demonstration. Once all four steps have been computationally demonstrated, the session is complete.
